title: CORS allows every HTTP method from any origin
description: The Access-Control-Allow-Methods response header declares a wildcard, so a browser preflight accepts any method the resource implements from any origin. Combined with a permissive origin policy this widens the set of cross-origin calls a page can make. The check reads the declared method list; it does not claim that a state-changing method is actually reachable.
remediation: List the methods the API actually serves (for example GET, POST, OPTIONS) and keep the origin allowlist explicit.
limitation: Observation-level: evaluates the Access-Control-Allow-Methods header alone. Whether a dangerous method is implemented, and whether credentials are allowed, requires separate evidence.
